definition: eight beds and eight fruit trees giving under one per cent of what we eat

settled:
We have eight raised beds, four feet by eight each, and eight fruit trees, six of them mature and two newly planted.

That is not a dependency on anybody. It is a capability we own.

It gives under one per cent of what the household eats.

The bottleneck is not the infrastructure. It is the harvest-and-preserve workflow, what to plant when, and the rhythm of actually working it.

The capital is already spent, so ramping the yield up costs effort rather than money. Jen cooks and preserves at a professional level, and that is the half of the household that closes the gap when there is bandwidth for it.

It is the highest-leverage move I have toward feeding ourselves.

title: The Garden We Do Not Eat From
